This small example runs entirely on your computer with invented records. No
connection, credentials or clinical data are needed. Run one chunk at a time and
change the code lists or dates. These codes illustrate matching, not validated
clinical definitions or a study protocol.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

[Guide index](start-here.html) | Guide 5 of 5

The detailed contracts are in [time windows](look-back-follow-up.html) and
[condition flags](condition-flags.html). Here we put those operations together.

## 1. Make a tiny source

```{r records}
library(thipR)
library(dplyr)

visits <- tibble::tibble(
  person = c("A", "A", "A", "B", "B", "C", "C"),
  adm = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2022-01-10", "2023-02-01",
                  "2019-06-01", "2020-01-01", "2020-01-01", "2020-06-01")),
  pdx = c("K35.8", "F12.1", "F20.0", "F20.0", "K35.8", "K35.8", "J06.9")
)
visits
```

## 2. Choose candidate entries

For local data, use `icd_flag()` and ordinary filtering. Here one entry is the
first recorded appendicitis admission per person, and time zero is the next day.
A real study must specify admission/discharge timing and eligibility itself.

```{r candidates}
visits <- visits |> mutate(record_id = row_number())
entry_flags <- icd_flag(
  visits, conditions = list(appendicitis = "K35"),
  id = "record_id", cols = "pdx", match = "prefix"
)

entries <- visits |>
  left_join(entry_flags, by = "record_id") |>
  filter(appendicitis == TRUE) |>
  arrange(person, adm) |>
  distinct(person, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  transmute(person, entry_id = record_id, index_date = adm + 1L)
entries
```

`icd_flag()` returns flags rather than modifying its input. Dots, surrounding
spaces and case are normalized. `match = "exact"` is the default; use `"prefix"`
explicitly when subcodes should match.

## 3. Draw a history window

```{r history}
history <- thip_window(
  visits, entries, by = "person", date = "adm",
  index = "index_date", window = c(-365L, 0L)
) |>
  collect()
history
```

This history window includes day −365 and excludes day 0.

## 4. Flag history and choose the cohort

```{r cohort}
history_flags <- icd_flag(
  history, conditions = list(prior_psychosis = paste0("F", 20:29)),
  id = "entry_id", cols = "pdx", match = "prefix"
)

screened <- entries |> left_join(history_flags, by = "entry_id")
cohort <- screened |> filter(prior_psychosis == FALSE)
cohort
```

Person B is excluded by this example's rule. An `NA` flag means all selected
codes were blank/missing; an unmatched entry also becomes `NA` after the join.
Neither is silently treated as negative. `FALSE` means recorded nonmatching
codes, not proof of disease absence. More detailed quality rules belong in the
study, rather than being inferred by `icd_flag()`.

## 5. Follow retained people through a study end

Use explicit dates for follow-up that can span several years. Source records
must actually cover the period; setting a window does not create observation.

```{r followup}
followup_windows <- cohort |>
  mutate(followup_start = index_date,
         followup_end = as.Date("2024-01-01"))

followup <- thip_window(
  visits, followup_windows, by = "person", date = "adm",
  start = "followup_start", end = "followup_end"
) |>
  collect(batch_size = 100L)
followup
```

## 6. Flag conditions visibly

```{r flags}
conditions <- list(cannabis = c("F12.1", "F12.2"), psychosis = "F20")
flags <- icd_flag(
  followup, conditions, id = "record_id", cols = "pdx", match = "prefix"
)
followup <- followup |> left_join(flags, by = "record_id")
followup
```

Here we flag by source record, then attach the flags to its entry window.

## 7. Summarize first dates with ordinary R code

```{r results}
cannabis_dates <- followup |>
  filter(cannabis == TRUE) |>
  group_by(entry_id) |>
  summarise(cannabis_date = min(adm), .groups = "drop")
psychosis_dates <- followup |>
  filter(psychosis == TRUE) |>
  group_by(entry_id) |>
  summarise(psychosis_date = min(adm), .groups = "drop")

results <- cohort |>
  left_join(cannabis_dates, by = "entry_id") |>
  left_join(psychosis_dates, by = "entry_id") |>
  mutate(days_cannabis_to_psychosis =
           as.integer(psychosis_date - cannabis_date))
results
```

Person A enters in 2020, has cannabis recorded in 2022 and psychosis in 2023.
Person C stays in the result without either event. The final table contains
**descriptive recorded-event dates**, not a survival-analysis specification.
Death censoring, exposure transitions and eligibility need explicit study rules;
future exposure should not be assigned as a baseline characteristic.

## Use a remote source

See [from question to cohort](question-to-cohort.html) for `thip_table()` and
`thip_filter_icd()`. Candidate records enter R at `collect()`; `thip_window()`
then retrieves each person's records through another explicit `collect()`.
The same ID must link across source years. Source coverage, eligibility and
missing-data rules remain study decisions.
